summary: Claims glitches on soc_dbg_policy_d in SocDbgStProd from a cross-clock-domain shadow register can transiently switch the debug policy. The shadowed register and the policy combinational logic are all in the single clk_i domain, and the distributed policy is the registered soc_dbg_policy_q, not the combinational _d, so no glitch reaches consumers.
root_cause: No defect. In soc_dbg_ctrl.sv:127-149 the prim_subreg_shadow (u_debug_policy_category_shadowed) is clocked by clk_i (the same clock as the always_comb at line 180 and the always_ff at line 217). There is no second clock domain. The combinational soc_dbg_policy_d (line 203-206) is registered into soc_dbg_policy_q at line 223 and only soc_dbg_policy_q is distributed (soc_dbg_policy_bus_o = soc_dbg_policy_q, line 228), so any combinational settling on _d is filtered by the flop.
reasoning: soc_dbg_ctrl.sv:30-34 shows all interfaces (clk_i and the LC/boot inputs) are single-clock. The shadow register at lines 127-149 uses clk_i/rst_ni. soc_dbg_policy_d at line 181-214 is purely combinational and is sampled by the synchronous always_ff at 217-225, producing soc_dbg_policy_q which feeds the SoC bus at line 228. There is no asynchronous crossing. formal field has empty SVA / status NO_PROPERTY (not run).
formal_alignment: N/A (formal status NO_PROPERTY, no property generated)

summary: Claims that if NumAlerts > 2 the upper bits of alert_tx_o are undriven. NumAlerts is a fixed localparam = 2 in the reg package and the generate loop instantiates a prim_alert_sender for every index i < NumAlerts, driving every alert_tx_o[i]. The >2 scenario is not reachable.
root_cause: No defect. soc_dbg_ctrl_reg_pkg.sv:10 defines `parameter int NumAlerts = 2` (it is a generated constant, not overridable). soc_dbg_ctrl.sv:66-80 `for (genvar i = 0; i < NumAlerts; i++)` instantiates one prim_alert_sender per i and connects `.alert_tx_o(alert_tx_o[i])`, so all NumAlerts outputs are driven. There is no configuration in which NumAlerts > 2 with bits left undriven.
reasoning: The generate loop bound equals the array width (alert_tx_o is [NumAlerts-1:0], line 20), so every element is driven. The alert[] and IsFatal[] arrays (lines 61-65) are sized to NumAlerts=2 and fully assigned. The finding's premise (NumAlerts>2) cannot occur. formal status PENDING (not actually run).
formal_alignment: N/A (formal status PENDING, property not evaluated)

summary: Expresses uncertainty about the internal error detection of the PRIM_FLOP_SPARSE_FSM macro and halt_state behavior. The macro is the standard OpenTitan sparse-FSM security countermeasure; the RTL provides defensive handling and an alert, so there is no defect.
root_cause: No defect. soc_dbg_ctrl.sv:378-379 instantiates `PRIM_FLOP_SPARSE_FSM(u_state_regs, halt_state_d, halt_state_q, halt_state_e, Idle)` (SEC_CM: HALT.FSM.SPARSE). The always_comb default case (lines 371-374) sets halt_fsm_err=1 on any illegal state, and line 406 routes that to alert_tx_o[0] via ASSERT_PRIM_FSM_ERROR_TRIGGER_ALERT. The macro is a well-defined library primitive providing sparse-encoding error detection.
reasoning: The 'invisible macro' concern is resolved: it is a standard prim providing FSM-tamper detection. The combination of the sparse encoding (soc_dbg_ctrl_pkg.sv:75-83), the default-case error flag, and the alert binding constitutes the intended defensive design. formal status NO_PROPERTY.

summary: Notes alert_ack_o and alert_state_o on the prim_alert_sender are left unconnected. These are optional status outputs of the standard alert sender and are intentionally tied open across OpenTitan; this is deliberate, not an oversight.
root_cause: No defect. soc_dbg_ctrl.sv:75-76 leaves `.alert_ack_o()` and `.alert_state_o()` open on the prim_alert_sender instance. These outputs are not required by soc_dbg_ctrl and are conventionally unconnected in OpenTitan alert wiring; the functional alert handshake is carried entirely by alert_rx_i/alert_tx_o (lines 77-78).
reasoning: Leaving optional sender status outputs open is standard practice and does not affect the alert protocol, which uses alert_tx_o/alert_rx_i. This is a self-referential uncertainty finding with no specs/evidence; RTL inspection shows intentional design.

summary: Claims that in SocDbgStProd, X/illegal shadowed-register values propagate to soc_dbg_policy_d with no error detection, masking, or fallback. In reality the shadow register has storage/update error detection wired to alerts, and the downstream decoder uses strict MuBi/category tests so illegal values resolve to the locked/no-debug (fail-safe) condition.
root_cause: No defect. The category source u_debug_policy_category_shadowed (soc_dbg_ctrl.sv:127-149) emits policy_shadowed_storage_err / policy_shadowed_update_err, which feed alert[0]/alert[1] (lines 61-63). Downstream, soc_dbg_ctrl_decode.sv:57-58,94-100 decodes valid/relocked with mubi4_test_true_strict and category by exact enum compare, so any X/illegal value yields cat*_dbg_o=0 (locked) and relocked/valid=false — fail-closed.
reasoning: Error detection exists (shadow err -> alerts). Masking/fallback exists in the consumer: an illegal category does not match DbgCategory2/3/4 (soc_dbg_ctrl_decode.sv:95-100) so it grants no debug; illegal valid fails the strict mubi test (line 57). The module does not need to also mask inside the always_comb because the secure consumer already fails closed.

summary: Claims the always_comb case may have a missing branch leaving soc_dbg_policy_d holding soc_dbg_policy_q. Every case branch including default fully assigns all three fields, so the initial hold-assignment is always overwritten.
root_cause: No defect. In soc_dbg_ctrl.sv:183-214 the `unique case (soc_dbg_state_i)` has branches SocDbgStBlank (184-192), SocDbgStPreProd (194-198), SocDbgStProd (202-207) and default (209-213). Each branch assigns category, valid and relocked. The default case covers all remaining encodings, so soc_dbg_policy_d is always fully driven; the line-181 `= soc_dbg_policy_q` initializer only serves to avoid latch inference.
reasoning: There is no soc_dbg_state_i value that escapes the case because default exists, and every field is assigned in every branch. The unintended-hold scenario cannot occur. formal status NO_PROPERTY.

summary: Claims boot_status_i is assumed stable while lc_dft_en_i=1 with no internal glitch defense. boot_status_i is a synchronous same-clock-domain input from pwrmgr; its sampling is into synchronous registers/FSM, so the stability assumption is a normal synchronous-input contract, not a defect.
root_cause: No defect. boot_status_i (soc_dbg_ctrl.sv:34, type pwrmgr_pkg::pwr_boot_status_t) is driven by the pwrmgr in the same io_div4 clock domain (comment line 308 confirms shared clk). It is consumed by synchronous logic (always_ff FSM via halt_state, and combinational assignments registered downstream). No CDC exists, so no synchronizer/glitch filter is required inside this module.
reasoning: Same-domain inputs are expected to be stable around the clock edge per normal synchronous design; the absence of an internal synchronizer is correct, not a gap. The finding is an upstream-contract assumption. formal status PENDING (not run).

summary: Duplicate of F-0005: claims X/illegal shadowed values in SocDbgStProd bypass debug access control via soc_dbg_policy_d. Shadow-register error detection plus strict fail-closed decoding prevent any bypass.
root_cause: No defect. Same path as F-0005: soc_dbg_ctrl.sv:202-207 sources policy from the shadowed category register (with storage/update error -> alerts, lines 147-148, 61-63) and from valid/relocked register q-fields. The consumer soc_dbg_ctrl_decode.sv:57-58,95-100 uses strict MuBi and exact-enum tests, so corrupted values yield no debug grant (fail-closed).
reasoning: An illegal category cannot match DbgCategory2/3/4 and therefore grants nothing; an illegal valid fails mubi4_test_true_strict. There is no scenario where corrupted shadow values open debug. formal status NAME_UNVERIFIED (property not actually run).

summary: Claims continue_cpu_boot_o.done might be dropped during HaltDone. The RTL drives done=MuBi4True as a stable level in the HaltDone state, which is an absorbing state, so done is held continuously while in HaltDone.
root_cause: No defect. soc_dbg_ctrl.sv:323 defaults continue_cpu_boot_o.done=MuBi4False, and the HaltDone branch (lines 366-369) sets continue_cpu_boot_o.done=MuBi4True. HaltDone has no exit transition (it stays until reset), so done is asserted as a level for the entire duration of HaltDone. continue_cpu_boot_o.good is permanently MuBi4True (line 306).
reasoning: Because done is combinationally driven from halt_state_q==HaltDone and HaltDone is absorbing, done cannot be accidentally dropped. The 'consumer expects pulse' risk is hypothetical; the design intent (level) is consistent. formal_verdict DIRECT but status was not actually executed (DIRECT here is a formalizability label).
formal_alignment: Aligned: the property (HaltDone |-> done==MuBi4True) holds in the RTL.

summary: Claims halt_cpu_boot_sync and jtag_control.q are used in next-state logic without synchronization, risking glitch-induced illegal transitions. Both are registered/synchronized signals, so they are glitch-free at the clock edge.
root_cause: No defect. halt_cpu_boot_sync is the output of prim_flop_2sync (soc_dbg_ctrl.sv:309-317), i.e. a two-stage synchronized register output. jtag_reg2hw.jtag_control.q is a register field from u_jtag_reg (line 102-111), synchronous to clk_i. Both feed the always_comb FSM (lines 350-364) as stable registered values, so no glitch/metastability path into next-state exists.
reasoning: The synchronizer at lines 310-317 explicitly addresses the asynchronous halt_cpu_boot_i pin; the FSM consumes only the synchronized version. jtag_control comes from a TL-UL register, inherently synchronous. The premise of unsynchronized comb inputs is incorrect. formal status NO_PROPERTY.

summary: Claims the FSM can block forever in Idle if boot_status_i.lc_done never arrives. Waiting in Idle for lc_done is the intended boot-sequence design; lc_done is guaranteed by the lifecycle/power-up sequence, and never booting is the safe outcome if it does not arrive.
root_cause: No defect. soc_dbg_ctrl.sv:326-330 keeps halt_state_q in Idle until boot_status_i.lc_done is high, then advances to CheckLifecycleState. This is the deliberate gating of the debug-boot sequence on lifecycle completion. lc_done is produced by the pwrmgr during normal power-up; its absence means the SoC has not completed boot, in which case staying halted is correct (fail-safe).
reasoning: This is a liveness assumption on a correctly-functioning upstream (pwrmgr/lc_ctrl), not an RTL defect. The module cannot and should not force lc_done. formal_verdict was a cover property (liveness), status NAME_UNVERIFIED, not run.

summary: Claims non-default states lack a legality guarantee for soc_dbg_policy_d.relocked, risking illegal encodings being stored and misinterpreted. In Blank/PreProd/default, relocked is hardcoded to the legal MuBi4False; only in Prod is it sourced from a register, and the consumer decodes it fail-closed.
root_cause: No defect. soc_dbg_ctrl.sv assigns soc_dbg_policy_d.relocked = MuBi4False in SocDbgStBlank (line 191), SocDbgStPreProd (197) and default (212). In SocDbgStProd (line 206) relocked comes from core_reg2hw.debug_policy_relocked.q. Any non-strict value is treated as not-relocked by the consumer soc_dbg_ctrl_decode.sv:58,94 (mubi4_test_true_strict), so it cannot be misinterpreted as a valid relock that bypasses security.
reasoning: All hardcoded branches use legal MuBi4 constants; the register-sourced Prod value is consumed with strict tests. There is no path where an illegal relocked encoding produces an unsafe grant. formal_verdict DIRECT (formalizability label) but not actually executed.
formal_alignment: Aligned: relocked/valid take legal MuBi4 values in all states except the register-driven Prod case, which is decoded safely.

summary: Claims a deadlock if lc_dft_en_i is never asserted while in Wait4DftEn. Holding in Wait4DftEn until volatile raw unlock (lc_dft_en) is the intended secure behavior; remaining halted denies debug, which is fail-safe, not a bug.
root_cause: No defect. soc_dbg_ctrl.sv:341-348: in Wait4DftEn the FSM advances to CheckHaltPin only when lc_tx_test_true_strict(lc_dft_en_i) is true; otherwise it waits. The comment (lines 342-344) documents this as waiting for Volatile Raw Unlock. If unlock never occurs the CPU stays halted, which is the secure default for a RAW/locked lifecycle state.
reasoning: The 'deadlock' is intentional fail-closed behavior gated on a lifecycle authorization signal. The module cannot self-assert lc_dft_en. formal_verdict PARTIAL, status PENDING (not run).

summary: Claims the reset default DbgCategoryLocked conflicts with PreProd needing DbgCategory4 in the first post-reset cycle. Starting locked is the secure (fail-closed) default; the combinational logic computes the correct category and it is registered on the next clock, and valid starts False so no debug is granted during the one-cycle window.
root_cause: No defect. soc_dbg_ctrl.sv:218-221 resets soc_dbg_policy_q to category=DbgCategoryLocked, valid=MuBi4False, relocked=MuBi4False. On the first clock after reset, soc_dbg_policy_d is recomputed from soc_dbg_state_i (lines 183-214) and captured into _q. The transient locked/invalid state denies debug, which is strictly safer than the steady-state policy; there is no functional error.
reasoning: valid=MuBi4False at reset means the consumer (soc_dbg_ctrl_decode) grants nothing until valid is set, so the one-cycle Locked default cannot open debug or break functionality. A locked-then-correct sequence is the intended fail-safe ordering. formal_verdict DIRECT but not executed.
formal_alignment: N/A (property references reset-cycle behavior; not actually evaluated)

summary: Claims soc_dbg_policy_d.category is stored without legality validation, allowing an illegal enum injection that bypasses security. In Prod the category comes from a shadowed register (write-gated and integrity-checked), and the consumer treats any non-Cat2/3/4 value as locked (no debug).
root_cause: No defect. The Prod category source is the shadowed register (soc_dbg_ctrl.sv:127-149), writable by SW only when not_valid (line 137) and protected by storage/update error detection -> alerts. Even an illegal category value is fail-closed at the consumer: soc_dbg_ctrl_decode.sv:95-100 only grants cat4/cat3/cat2 for exact enum matches, so any reserved/illegal encoding yields no debug access.
reasoning: Storing an illegal category does not grant anything because debug grants require exact category matches AND a valid/strict mubi. The 'silent storage' of an illegal value has no security effect. formal_verdict NONE, partial SVA references undefined legal-set macro (not run).

summary: Claims continue_cpu_boot_o.valid and .value are unassigned, leaving X. The output type pwrmgr_data_t has only two fields (done, good); there are no valid or value fields, so the finding's premise is wrong and both real fields are driven.
root_cause: No defect (finding premise incorrect). continue_cpu_boot_o is rom_ctrl_pkg::pwrmgr_data_t (soc_dbg_ctrl.sv:39), defined as a packed struct of exactly {mubi4_t done; mubi4_t good;} in rom_ctrl_pkg.sv:11-14. Both fields are driven: good=MuBi4True (line 306) and done in the FSM always_comb (lines 323, 368). No valid/value fields exist.
reasoning: The ASSERT_KNOWN(ContinueBootKnown_A, continue_cpu_boot_o) at line 399 further guarantees the whole struct is known. The finding assumed extra fields that the type does not contain. formal status NO_PROPERTY.

summary: Claims the debug policy might not be connected to core_hw2reg/jtag_hw2reg or that the de enables might not be constant 1. The RTL explicitly assigns all trace fields with de hardwired to 1'b1, sourcing the registered soc_dbg_policy_q.
root_cause: No defect. soc_dbg_ctrl.sv:236-248 assigns core_hw2reg.trace_debug_policy_category.{de=1'b1, d=soc_dbg_policy_q.category}, the valid/relocked subfields with de=1'b1, and the identical jtag_hw2reg.* mappings. All de fields are literal 1'b1 and the data is the registered policy, so the trace is always exposed and connected.
reasoning: The connections exist and de is constant 1 by construction. The finding uses soc_dbg_policy_d in its SVA, but the RTL correctly uses the registered soc_dbg_policy_q for trace; the trace mirrors the actual distributed policy. No observability gap. formal_verdict NONE, NAME_UNVERIFIED (not run).

summary: Claims mubi4_test_true_strict behavior on invalid rom_ctrl_status could forge done/good and falsify boot integrity. The strict test returns true only for the exact MuBi4True encoding; any invalid/corrupted value resolves to false, which is fail-safe and cannot forge a good/done report.
root_cause: No defect. soc_dbg_ctrl.sv:273-284 maps boot_status_i.rom_ctrl_status[*].done/good through mubi4_test_true_strict into jtag_boot_status fields. mubi4_test_true_strict (prim_mubi_pkg) returns 1 only when the input exactly equals MuBi4True; all other patterns (including corrupted/invalid) return 0. Thus corruption can only downgrade a report (true->false), never forge a passing status.
reasoning: Strict MuBi testing is the OpenTitan fail-safe idiom: it cannot mask an error into a 'good' result. The report is conservative under corruption. formal status NO_PROPERTY.

summary: Claims missing guarantee that relocked decodes correctly, with a premise that MuBi True/False are 4'b1111/4'b0000. The decode logic is correct (relocked_decoded = strict-true test), and the finding's stated encodings are wrong (MuBi4 uses 4'h6/4'h9, not 1111/0000).
root_cause: No defect. soc_dbg_ctrl_decode.sv:58 assigns relocked_decoded = mubi4_test_true_strict(relocked), which is 1 exactly when relocked == MuBi4True. So when relocked is MuBi4True, relocked_decoded is 1 as required. The finding's SVA premise (4'b1111 -> 1) misstates the MuBi4 encoding but the actual strict decode is functionally correct.
reasoning: The decode fully partitions the input space (strict-true -> 1, else 0), and relocked_o=valid_decoded & relocked_decoded (line 94) further requires valid. There is no missing-decode case. formal_verdict DIRECT but status INCOMPLETE (no clock) -> not actually proven; manual analysis confirms correctness.

summary: Claims that with SyncDbgPolicy=0 and SampleValidOnce=1 an async glitch on valid can create multiple valid_rising pulses and over-sample. SyncDbgPolicy is an explicit configuration knob: when the bus is asynchronous the integrator sets SyncDbgPolicy=1 to add synchronizers; the edge detector also samples synchronously, so this is a documented configuration tradeoff, not a defect.
root_cause: No defect. soc_dbg_ctrl_decode.sv:25-54 provides a SyncDbgPolicy generate branch with prim_flop_2sync synchronizers for exactly the asynchronous-source case; the async branch (line 51-54) is selected only when the integrator declares the source synchronous. The valid_rising pulse (lines 62-70) is produced by prim_edge_detector, whose internal flop (prim_edge_detector.sv:47-52) registers the comparison, so en_i to the sample flop is evaluated synchronously at clk_i.
reasoning: The parameterization is the design's answer to CDC: choosing SyncDbgPolicy=0 is a contract that the source is synchronous. Within the module the sampling is synchronous. This is intended configurability, consistent with OpenTitan CDC practice. formal_verdict PARTIAL, status PENDING (not run).

summary: Claims an invalid MuBi encoding of lc_raw_test_rma_i (from SEU) could cause lc_tx_test_true_strict to misbehave and corrupt the halt FSM. The strict lc_tx test resolves any non-On value to false, sending the FSM to the safe HaltDone path; the lc_tx input is also already synchronized by lc_ctrl.
root_cause: No defect. soc_dbg_ctrl.sv:332-339 (CheckLifecycleState) uses lc_tx_test_true_strict(lc_raw_test_rma_i): only an exact lc_tx On selects the Wait4DftEn (unlock) path; any other/invalid value selects HaltDone. An SEU-corrupted value therefore biases toward the more-restrictive HaltDone, not toward granting unauthorized access.
reasoning: lc_tx_test_true_strict is the OpenTitan fail-safe decoder; corrupted lc_tx values resolve to false. lc_raw_test_rma_i originates from lc_ctrl (synchronized). The finding has no specs/evidence and is self-referential. formal status NO_PROPERTY.

summary: Notes that rom_ctrl_status[2].good's MuBi false is not distinguished from corrupted values, and a future default change could break the legal-false case. This is a hypothetical future-change concern; current strict-true decoding is correct and fail-safe.
root_cause: No defect. soc_dbg_ctrl.sv:283-284 uses mubi4_test_true_strict(boot_status_i.rom_ctrl_status[2].good); legal-false and corrupted both yield 0, which is the intended conservative reporting. There is no current functional error; the finding only speculates about a possible future semantic change.
reasoning: Collapsing false and illegal to 'not-true' is the deliberate fail-safe contract for boot status reporting. No current defect. Self-referential finding, no specs/evidence. formal status NO_PROPERTY.

summary: Questions whether SocDbgStBlank unconditionally setting DbgCategory4 (when dft/debug_en) is legal in production. This exactly matches the documented policy table in the RTL header; Blank is an early-lifecycle state and the behavior is specified, not a gap.
root_cause: No defect. soc_dbg_ctrl.sv:184-192 implements the documented table at lines 167-175: SocDbgStBlank with lc_dft_en or lc_hw_debug_en true -> DbgCategory4, else DbgCategoryLocked. This is the intended behavior; in PROD lifecycle these LC enables are not asserted, so Blank+enable does not arise in production.
reasoning: The implementation faithfully follows the in-file policy table. Granting Category4 in Blank requires lc_dft_en/lc_hw_debug_en (lifecycle-authorized), so it is gated by the lifecycle controller. formal_verdict PARTIAL (cover), status NAME_UNVERIFIED (not run).

summary: Questions whether exposing soc_dbg_state_i unfiltered to JTAG (when lc_dft_en_i true) leaks sensitive state. The exposure is gated by lc_dft_en (test/DFT mode) and is intended debug observability of a coarse lifecycle debug-state value.
root_cause: No defect. soc_dbg_ctrl.sv:265,285 expose jtag_hw2reg.jtag_trace_soc_dbg_state.d = soc_dbg_state_i only inside the lc_tx_test_true_strict(lc_dft_en_i) guard; outside DFT the field is forced to 0 (line 263). soc_dbg_state_i is the public SoC debug-state encoding, intended to be observable for debug.
reasoning: Exposure is conditioned on DFT/test authorization; this is intended observability, not a leak. UNCERTAIN in the finding because no spec defines sensitivity, but RTL shows the access is gated and the data is non-secret state. formal status NO_PROPERTY.

summary: Questions leaking halt_state_q to JTAG without sanitization. The exposure is gated by lc_dft_en (test mode) and is intended FSM observability; the FSM state is not secret.
root_cause: No defect. soc_dbg_ctrl.sv:270 assigns jtag_hw2reg.jtag_boot_status.halt_fsm_state = halt_state_q, but only inside the lc_tx_test_true_strict(lc_dft_en_i) block (line 265); outside DFT it is 0 (line 262). Exposing the halt FSM state in DFT mode is intended debug visibility.
reasoning: The access is lifecycle-gated to DFT/test. The finding's SVA (jtag != halt_state under dft) is logically inverted and would be a wrong property. The halt FSM encoding is not security-sensitive. formal_verdict NONE, NAME_UNVERIFIED (not run).

summary: Questions whether multi-bit integrity of valid/relocked is checked, fearing a glitch could inject an invalid MuBi. The consumer decodes valid/relocked with strict MuBi tests so any invalid encoding fails closed; in non-Prod states they are hardwired to legal constants.
root_cause: No defect. valid/relocked are MuBi4 fields driven as legal constants in Blank/PreProd/default (soc_dbg_ctrl.sv:190-191,196-197,211-212) and from registers in Prod (204-206). The consumer soc_dbg_ctrl_decode.sv:57-58 applies mubi4_test_true_strict, so an invalid encoding resolves to false (no grant). The category path additionally has shadow-register integrity checking.
reasoning: Strict MuBi decoding provides the integrity-to-decision safety: invalid -> false. A separate explicit MuBi integrity checker is not required for correctness/security here. formal status NO_PROPERTY.

summary: Speculates that halt_cpu_boot_sync used by downstream logic could bypass security if it carries a spurious value. It is a synchronized signal used only inside the halt FSM, whose transitions are fail-safe; there is no security bypass path.
root_cause: No defect. halt_cpu_boot_sync (soc_dbg_ctrl.sv:309-317) is the synchronized halt pin, consumed only in CheckHaltPin (lines 350-357) to decide CheckJtagGo vs HaltDone. Neither branch grants debug; it only sequences the boot-halt handshake. It does not gate the debug policy or authentication.
reasoning: The signal is synchronized and its only effect is the halt/continue boot sequencing, which is independent of the debug-policy authorization path. No bypass exists. Self-referential finding, no concrete claim. formal status NO_PROPERTY.

summary: Speculates a glitch on soc_dbg_policy_q could be captured into the always-enabled trace registers. soc_dbg_policy_q is a synchronous register output (glitch-free), and the trace registers sample it synchronously.
root_cause: No defect. soc_dbg_policy_q is produced by the always_ff at soc_dbg_ctrl.sv:217-225 and is a stable registered value. The trace assignments (lines 236-248) copy soc_dbg_policy_q into hw2reg fields with de=1, sampled by the synchronous register blocks. A register-to-register synchronous path cannot capture a glitch.
reasoning: Because soc_dbg_policy_q is itself a flop output in clk_i, there is no metastability/glitch to capture; de=1 simply continuously mirrors a stable value. The finding's concern presupposes an unstable _q, which does not occur. formal status NO_PROPERTY.

summary: Requires that the Idle parameter be a valid sparse-FSM reset-state encoding. Idle is a defined member of the sparse-encoded halt_state_e and is passed as the reset state to PRIM_FLOP_SPARSE_FSM, so this holds.
root_cause: No defect. soc_dbg_ctrl_pkg.sv:77 defines Idle = 6'b101000 within the halt_state_e sparse encoding (generated by sparse-fsm-encode.py, min Hamming distance 3, lines 56-83). soc_dbg_ctrl.sv:379 passes Idle as the reset state to PRIM_FLOP_SPARSE_FSM, and the always_ff/macro reset halt_state_q to Idle. The encoding is a legal sparse state.
reasoning: Idle is one of the six sparse-encoded states and is the designated reset state; this satisfies the assumption. formal_verdict PARTIAL, status NO_PROPERTY (not run); manual check confirms.

summary: Empty/contentless coverage finding on halt_state_d citing only invisible-macro uncertainty. The FSM next-state logic fully drives halt_state_d across all states with a defensive default, so there is no coverage gap or defect.
root_cause: No defect. soc_dbg_ctrl.sv:319-376: halt_state_d defaults to halt_state_q (line 321) and every legal state branch assigns the proper next state; the default branch sets halt_fsm_err (line 373). The PRIM_FLOP_SPARSE_FSM (line 379) provides tamper detection. There is no missing drive.
reasoning: The finding has no specs/evidence and references only macro invisibility. RTL inspection shows complete next-state coverage and defensive default. formal status NO_PROPERTY.

summary: Empty coverage finding on halt_state_e claiming undefined legal-value set. The halt_state_e enum is fully defined with six sparse-encoded members and is exhaustively handled by the FSM case plus a defensive default.
root_cause: No defect. soc_dbg_ctrl_pkg.sv:76-83 defines halt_state_e with six members (Idle, CheckLifecycleState, Wait4DftEn, CheckHaltPin, CheckJtagGo, HaltDone). soc_dbg_ctrl.sv:325-375 handles each, with default -> halt_fsm_err. The legal set and dispatch are well-defined.
reasoning: The enum and its handling are complete; the finding's 'no legal value set' premise is contradicted by the package. No specs/evidence in the finding. formal status NO_PROPERTY.

summary: Claims main_status/io_status assigned to jtag register .d fields may have a MuBi/encoded type mismatch. Both source and destination are plain 1-bit logic, so there is no type mismatch.
root_cause: No defect. boot_status_i.clk_status.main_status and .io_status are 1-bit `logic` (pwrmgr_pkg pwr_clk_rsp_t, lines 95-98).
